target: Reusable evidence base with domain-owned claim/check rules; authoring workflows are packaged separately, Endpoints is a consumer.
preservationStatus: Provisional; normalized from the source and explicit user requirements, not user-confirmed exact equivalence.

preservation.text: Reusable base mechanisms are separate from domain semantic rules and authoring workflows.
A requirement remains visible without evidence; useful partial evidence does not close its remainder.
Alternatives may establish one premise; every conjunctive premise must hold.
Evidence applies to named claims and contexts, with shared compatible uses and explicit freshness.
preservation.basis: source: L2/L3; R22 as captured in source

preservation.text: A directly reported relevant counterexample cannot be erased by newer unrelated passes; repair exercises the same failure.
Run identity, individual observations, agent interpretation and consumer permission remain distinct.
Unknown support does not secretly choose a strictness policy; actual contradiction stays visible.
Evidence inputs include code, data, environment, configuration, methods and external dependencies; recorded context is not proof of capture completeness.
Shared tasks and shared semantic blind spots can be explained without turning counts into confidence.
Checks and inference rules have a declared trust boundary; empirical passes do not silently become universal proofs.
preservation.basis: user-required: claim-specific proof systems; analyst inference about admission boundary

preservation.text: No code reversion renews an old test; rubric-only reassessment is distinct; check startup failure stays a CI error.
The base does not require a graph product, theorem prover, authentication rewrite or live-client recovery.
preservation.basis: source: arrangements and rejected recombinations; user base target

primitives.text: Claim: a versioned predicate about a subject under explicit conditions. A requested claim exists before support.
primitives.job: States both goals and intermediate premises; carries the uncovered requirement.
primitives.ablation: Without it evidence can be attached but no exact obligation or remainder is identifiable.

primitives.text: Observation: an immutable reported result tied to one execution, method, origin and captured context.
primitives.job: Separates observed outcome from inferred conclusion. Run metadata can be shared.
primitives.ablation: Without it arguments collapse the recorded event into a current interpretation; one run cannot preserve distinct outcomes.

primitives.text: Rule: a versioned, registered acceptance or inference procedure declaring its premises and side conditions.
primitives.job: Separates domain semantics from generic argument traversal.
primitives.ablation: Without it every proposed edge could grant support or all domain logic moves into the base.

primitives.text: Argument: a proposed application of a rule to observations and/or premise arguments for a claim.
primitives.job: Retains alternative support routes and their actual dependency paths.
primitives.ablation: Without it alternative methods and conjunctive obligations flatten into a bag of attachments.

primitives.text: Applicability condition: a rule-owned relation between captured and requested context, with explicit unknown results.
primitives.job: Supports compatible reuse, expiry and incomplete capture without equating hash equality with fresh observation.
primitives.ablation: Without it one observation can silently gain provider scope or stale evidence can regain support.

primitives.text: Challenge: a targeted objection or reported counterexample plus its unresolved/resolution history.
primitives.job: Separates speculative critique from an observed mismatch and prevents unrelated green results erasing it.
primitives.ablation: Without it monotone accumulation of green observations conceals compatible failures.

relations.text: An argument concludes one claim using a named rule.
Each required premise is a claim that needs a supported argument; arguments for the same claim are alternatives.
relations.ablation: Loses AND/OR distinction; allows one strong premise to replace another.

relations.text: An argument cites observations with their run and semantic dependencies.
relations.ablation: Loses measured outcomes and visible shared blind spots.

relations.text: Each use of evidence is assessed against the requested context and rule.
relations.ablation: Loses compatible reuse or admits invalid cross-scope transfer.

relations.text: A challenge targets a claim/use/inference and any resolution links the original challenge to later evidence.
relations.ablation: Loses original-failure identity or lets arbitrary newer passes clear a contradiction.

rules.text: Only registered rules can admit arguments; registered code remains a trusted semantic extension, not a theorem proved by the base.
rules.ablation: An agent can add a support edge that certifies itself.

rules.text: A rule application must establish every declared premise and side condition; any acceptable alternative argument may establish one premise. Cyclic support without independent grounding is insufficient.
rules.ablation: Conjunction, alternatives or finite grounding become unsound.

rules.text: Applicability is checked for each use. Unknown matching is unresolved rather than an invented proof of compatibility.
Original observations are not overwritten; new assessments/rules cannot rewrite what happened.
Code/context transitions can stale results; returning to prior bytes does not itself renew test evidence. Reassessment cannot renew stale observations.
rules.ablation: Code reversion silently reinstates stale authority.

rules.text: A relevant observed contradiction defeats support for the affected use and dependent arguments until an applicable resolution; unrelated passes do not resolve it. A conjectural critique remains a challenge, not a proved failure.
rules.ablation: A green alternative or agent dismissal bypasses a recorded counterexample.

rules.text: Repair resolution must identify the original law, case and observation and exercise that failure again. Different strategy or narrower scope must be separately justified.
rules.ablation: A different test can replace the failing obligation.

rules.text: Derive investigation work from uncovered premises; share compatible claims; tasks and notes do not grant support. Preserve the requested requirement when partial evidence arrives.
rules.ablation: Duplicates caller tasks or closes broad obligations after narrow findings.

rules.text: Return support, gaps and challenges independently of consumer permission and check severity.
rules.ablation: Unknown is silently turned into unconditional optimization veto or permission.

rules.text: Record each observation under its own measured law; neither origin nor a green aggregate grants unmeasured claims. A check unable to run yields an operational error outside the evidence history.
rules.ablation: Claims latency from read counts or records infrastructure failure as correctness evidence.

overlaps.text: A shared premise belongs to several argument paths; its gap and contradiction affect every applicable dependent use.
One observation/run may support multiple claims without merging their laws or acceptance rules.
Method/comparator/context dependencies overlap several checks; shared dependency is inspectable but not proof of a shared blind spot.

unresolved.text: Rule validity: the base can validate a declared procedure was used, not prove arbitrary plugin code sound.
Applicability/claim equivalence: exact identity is implementable; subsumption and semantic equivalence require domain rules.
Counterexample mapping across changed versions or strategies needs domain judgments; neither newest-wins nor global blocking is justified.
Missing-support severity and permission policy are deferred; support assessment must not choose them.
Complete context capture and hidden semantic dependency detection remain unsolved.
No proved hostile-process boundary is supplied by local APIs. Agents allowed to edit the runner can subvert it.
No total automatic investigation-priority order or generic proof search is derived.

boundaryConditions: Local trusted tooling; not a hostile-process security design.
Finite proposed arguments; no arbitrary theorem search.
Prototype may use exact identity and explicit context epochs, marking richer matching unsupported.
Source is a research arrangement, not a deployed evidence implementation.
